detailZh: F1大奖赛距离将在2027赛季缩短，同时比赛日将引入“硬性停止”时间。
2027年大奖赛距离将从305公里减至290公里；由于下赛季技术规则的变更，这一改变是必要的；从周四起在天空体育 F1直播阿塞拜疆大奖赛的每一节练习，正赛于周六中午12点举行。
国际汽联（FIA）已确认，2027赛季F1比赛的赛程距离将略有缩短。
在周一于伦敦举行的F1委员会会议上，这项运动的决策者同意将大奖赛距离从305公里减至290公里，根据赛道不同，相当于减少两到三圈。
做出这一改变是因为下赛季燃油流速将提高，这是FIA为优化2026年初引入的全新规则而采取的措施之一。

该决定必须得到世界汽车运动理事会的批准，但预计这只是一个形式。
FIA还宣布对因雨或其他因素中断比赛的协议进行轻微调整：取消从比赛开始到结束的三小时限制（包括中断），但引入任何赛车活动结束的“硬性停止”时间。

还确认将“在自由练习被中断时有更大的灵活性来延长练习时间”。
现行规则只允许在冲刺周末延长练习时间，但此类措施现在也可能在常规赛程中可用。

detailEn: F1 Grand Prix distances set to be reduced for 2027 season along with introduction of 'hard stop' time on race days

Grand Prix distances will be reduced from 305km to 290km in 2027; the change is required due to the alteration of technical regulations for next season; watch every session of the Azerbaijan GP from Thursday live on Sky Sports F1, with the race on Saturday at 12pm
There is set to be a slight reduction in the length of Formula 1 races for the 2027 season, the FIA has confirmed.

At a meeting of the F1 Commission in London on Monday, the sport's decision makers agreed to reduce Grand Prix distances from 305km to 290km, which corresponds to a reduction of two to three laps depending on the circuit.
The change is being made because fuel flow rates are being increased next season as part of measures the FIA are introducing to optimise the all-new regulations brought in at the start of 2026.

The FIA said: "In line with the refinements to the Power Unit regulations to be introduced in 2027 on fuel flow, a reduction in the total race distance from 305km to 290km was approved, corresponding to a reduction of two or three laps."
The decision must be approved by the World Motor Sport Council, but that is expected to be a formality.

The FIA also announced slight changes to protocols around races disrupted by rain or other factors, with a three-hour limit (including interruptions) from race to start to finish removed, but a "hard stop" time for the end of any racing activity to be introduced.
Highlights from the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix.
A limit of two hours of actual racing remains, with those decisions taken "to ensure that the spectators have the best possible chance to enjoy a full race if disruptions occur."
It was also confirmed that there will be "greater flexibility to extend Free Practice sessions should they be interrupted."
The current rules only allow for practice sessions to be extended on Sprint weekends, but such measures may now also be available on a regular schedule.

detailEn: United States GP: Lewis Hamilton fastest from Max Verstappen in final practice ahead of Qualifying in Austin

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton outpaced Red Bull's Max Verstappen in final practice in Austin with Friday's pace-setter Charles Leclerc in third; watch every United States GP session live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 10pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday
Lewis Hamilton claims the fastest lap from Max Verstappen in final practice at the United States Grand Prix
Lewis Hamilton topped final practice from Max Verstappen at the United States Grand Prix to set up a tantalising qualifying in Austin.
Hamilton was 0.168s quicker than Verstappen as Ferrari and Red Bull look set to fight for pole position and victory for a second consecutive weekend.
Charles Leclerc topped both of Friday's sessions and had set the quickest time in final practice by one tenth from Hamilton, only for it to be deleted due to track limits.

Track limits is set to be a major issue for the drivers in qualifying, which takes place at 10pm UK time later on Saturday (build-up from 8.30pm live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event) due to the tarmac run-off areas and the drivers keen to use every bit of track to gain lap time.

Leclerc still finished the session in third, ahead of championship leader Kimi Antonelli whose chances of becoming the youngest world champion look extremely difficult, given he must first win the Grand Prix to give himself an opportunity, and Mercedes are a tad off the pace.
Antonelli was three tenths behind Hamilton's pace-setting time with his Mercedes team-mate George Russell in fifth at nearly half a second down.

McLaren's Lando Norris was eighth but would have been in the top five had his best lap not been deleted for track limit, while Oscar Piastri was sixth and Audi's Nico Hulkenberg impressing in seventh.
